groups.rationale: Reviewed the native protocol reference after ADR-0186 replacement: v6/v3 provenance, all-false capabilities, unavailable artifact refusal and equal probe/readiness boot IDs are explicit. System responsibility, Ash ownership and deployed host topology remain unchanged.

Re-reviewed the settled distributed-revocation fixture: it selects the queued effect by call_id/tool and includes preparation in committed-fixture cleanup. This changes no production authorization, context commands or native admission behavior; existing chapters remain accurate. The scoped rerun recorded 16 passing checks (4 properties, 12 tests); it does not replace the earlier failed full Marshall execution or establish native machine acceptance.

Reviewed ADR-0186 native provenance, all-false capability schemas and bounded attestation. Guest/reference/scenario/security chapters distinguish target type checks and kernel-file identity from native boot evidence, and require equal kernel/readiness boot IDs.

Reviewed native image validation and the jail-local probe before credentials/readiness, including equal probe/readiness boot IDs. Guest/scenario/security chapters preserve jailer, network and ZFS boundaries and record absent native boot and recovery evidence under ADR-0186.

Reviewed native Lyra targets, the pinned fs2 illumos allocation fallback and source-only rc.d/SMF supervision. Service/agent/security chapters distinguish passed target type checks from absent linked images, start listeners before bounded SSH bootstrap and withhold readiness until live service checks succeed.

Reviewed native source and ABI receipts, zero-byte unavailable artifact guards and source-only image/service assembly in the current Nix layout. Deployment/guest/security chapters document fail-closed image construction, absent linked kernels/images and unchanged host topology; no native runtime acceptance is claimed.

Reviewed the expanded native architecture review for target type checks, pinned fs2 provenance and supervisor ordering. The mapped reference, coverage and security chapters already state all-false admission, kernel-file identity limits and absent native machine evidence; these review details add no further handbook behavior.
